claims.title: A holder of the fleet-wide key can flood the internet-facing gateway
claims.description: An attacker who obtains the fleet-wide pre-shared key from a node under physical control can publish a sustained volume of syntactically valid MQTT readings through `flow:sensor-node-to-device-gateway:publish-readings` to `process:device-gateway`. Because the key is shared by every device in a fleet, the gateway must perform authentication and device-registry lookup work for traffic that is cheap for the attacker to generate. This can exhaust the gateway's connections, worker capacity, or registry-request capacity and deny legitimate nodes access to the availability-critical ingest service. Second-order, accepted attack traffic is forwarded over `flow:device-gateway-to-telemetry-normalizer:forward-readings`, potentially backing up `process:telemetry-normalizer` and delaying legitimate telemetry loads into `store:telemetry-lake`. The model does not state per-device rate limits, MQTT connection limits, request-size bounds, or load shedding.

grounds.text: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway, which is an MQTT broker we run on GKE and expose to the internet because the nodes dial in from anywhere.
The key is per fleet, not per device. Nobody has rotated it since deployment.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium: the internet-facing `process:device-gateway` is reachable across `crossing:flow:sensor-node-to-device-gateway:publish-readings`, but the attacker must first obtain the fleet-wide key from a deployed node. Impact is high: `process:device-gateway` is tagged `availability-critical`, and saturation interrupts fleet ingest while propagating load to `process:telemetry-normalizer` and `store:telemetry-lake`.

mitigations.summary: Limit MQTT ingest per device and per fleet
mitigations.detail: Apply authenticated per-device connection, publish-rate, message-size, and in-flight-message limits at `process:device-gateway`; shed excess work before registry lookup and Pub/Sub publication.

mitigations.summary: Replace the fleet-wide key with revocable device credentials
mitigations.detail: Issue unique node credentials and support rotation and revocation, so compromise of one physically accessible node cannot provide sustained publish authority for its fleet.

mitigations.summary: Bound downstream propagation
mitigations.detail: Apply bounded Pub/Sub backlog, consumer concurrency limits, timeouts, and load shedding between `process:device-gateway` and `process:telemetry-normalizer`.

claims.title: Unauthenticated firmware downloads can exhaust the public bucket's serving capacity
claims.description: Any internet attacker can repeatedly request firmware images through `flow:sensor-node-to-firmware-bucket:poll-firmware`, which has explicitly absent authentication and crosses from the field network into `store:firmware-bucket`. Repeated or concurrent downloads are cheap to initiate but consume the bucket's request, bandwidth, and potentially metered egress capacity. If those shared limits are exhausted, deployed `entity:sensor-node` instances cannot retrieve legitimate updates; the model does not state rate limits, caching, download quotas, or capacity isolation for this public-read service.

grounds.text: The bucket is public read, because making the nodes authenticate to it was awkward.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high: authentication is stated absent on `flow:sensor-node-to-firmware-bucket:poll-firmware`, so any internet client can issue requests without credentials. Impact is medium: `store:firmware-bucket` holds business-critical firmware and an outage prevents fleet updates, but the model does not establish that normal telemetry operation immediately stops.

mitigations.summary: Constrain anonymous firmware-download demand
mitigations.detail: Apply request-rate and concurrent-download limits, response-size controls, and egress/request budget alarms for `store:firmware-bucket`, with capacity reserved for legitimate node polling.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate and authorize firmware retrieval
mitigations.detail: Give each node a scoped, rotatable download credential or time-limited signed retrieval authorization so limits can be enforced per device or fleet rather than against anonymous traffic.

claims.title: Unverified gateway-to-normalizer authentication may let an ingest-edge foothold invoke analytics authority
claims.description: `flow:device-gateway-to-telemetry-normalizer:forward-readings` crosses from `boundary:ingest-edge` to `boundary:analytics-core`, but its `authentication` is unknown. If `process:telemetry-normalizer` does not authenticate and authorize the gateway identity on that Pub/Sub path, an attacker who compromises the internet-facing `process:device-gateway` or obtains an ingest-edge foothold can publish work as an accepted gateway producer into the analytics core. The normalizer then processes that work under its own authority and writes it to `store:telemetry-lake` via `flow:telemetry-normalizer-to-telemetry-lake:load-readings`; the terminal capability is to cause unauthorized writes to the customer telemetry lake, rather than being confined to the ingest edge. This is conditional on the unstated authentication control on `flow:device-gateway-to-telemetry-normalizer:forward-readings`.

Impact is high because the resulting authority reaches `store:telemetry-lake`, which carries `pii` and `business-critical-data` customer telemetry.

claims.title: Unverified BigQuery writer identity may permit direct telemetry-lake corruption
claims.description: `flow:telemetry-normalizer-to-telemetry-lake:load-readings` performs writes to `store:telemetry-lake`, but its `authentication` is `unknown`. If this attribute resolves to missing or overly broad writer authorization, an attacker who reaches the BigQuery write interface can inject, overwrite, or backfill false site addresses, occupancy patterns, and readings directly into the lake, bypassing `process:telemetry-normalizer` validation. Second-order, `flow:fleet-operator-to-telemetry-lake:query-dashboards` exposes those forged records to `entity:fleet-operator` dashboards as customer telemetry. This claim is conditional on verification of the write identity and permissions.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:telemetry-normalizer-to-telemetry-lake:load-readings`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown writer authentication: reaching the internal analytics write path requires access or a foothold, but an absent or broad identity control would make modification straightforward. Impact is high because `store:telemetry-lake` holds customer data tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, and fleet operators consume its contents through `flow:fleet-operator-to-telemetry-lake:query-dashboards`.

mitigations.summary: Use a dedicated workload identity for lake writes
mitigations.detail: Resolve and enforce authentication on `flow:telemetry-normalizer-to-telemetry-lake:load-readings` using a short-lived identity unique to `process:telemetry-normalizer`.

mitigations.summary: Apply least-privilege BigQuery write permissions
mitigations.detail: Grant the normalizer only append or narrowly scoped write permissions for required tables and deny direct modification privileges to unrelated principals.

mitigations.summary: Make telemetry changes detectable
mitigations.detail: Use immutable ingestion records, versioning, and reconciliation checks so unauthorized overwrites or backfills in `store:telemetry-lake` are detectable and recoverable.

claims.title: Flooded accepted telemetry can consume shared telemetry-lake write and query capacity
claims.description: A party holding a fleet-wide node key can generate accepted readings that traverse `flow:sensor-node-to-device-gateway:publish-readings`, `flow:device-gateway-to-telemetry-normalizer:forward-readings`, and `flow:telemetry-normalizer-to-telemetry-lake:load-readings`. This turns cheap MQTT publishes into normalization and BigQuery write work at `store:telemetry-lake`. If ingestion throughput, storage budget, or BigQuery quotas are shared rather than bounded per fleet—a control posture not stated in the model—the attacker can consume capacity needed by `process:telemetry-normalizer` and by dashboard queries on `flow:fleet-operator-to-telemetry-lake:query-dashboards`. Second-order, legitimate ingest falls behind and `entity:fleet-operator` loses dashboard availability across the shared lake, which holds business-critical customer telemetry.

grounds.text: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub and picked up by the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network, which writes them into the telemetry lake in BigQuery.
Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

verdict.reason: The downstream denial-of-service claim depends on whether telemetry ingestion, storage, and BigQuery query capacity are shared across fleets or bounded and isolated; the model does not state that control posture.

related_unknowns.subject: Are Pub/Sub, telemetry-normalizer, BigQuery ingestion/storage, and dashboard-query quotas shared across fleets, or are they bounded and isolated per fleet?

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium: the attacker must obtain a fleet key and drive load through the gateway rather than access `store:telemetry-lake` directly, but the inbound route crosses into the platform via the cited crossings. Impact is medium: the shared `store:telemetry-lake` contains PII and business-critical data, and its saturation simultaneously delays telemetry writes and dashboard reads, though the described availability loss is recoverable.

mitigations.summary: Enforce fleet-scoped ingest and BigQuery budgets
mitigations.detail: Set per-fleet publish, normalization, BigQuery write, storage, and cost quotas so one fleet's readings cannot consume the capacity used by other ingest or dashboard workloads.

mitigations.summary: Bulkhead dashboard queries from ingestion
mitigations.detail: Reserve and separately meter capacity for `flow:fleet-operator-to-telemetry-lake:query-dashboards` and `flow:telemetry-normalizer-to-telemetry-lake:load-readings`, with bounded queues and fail-fast behavior when ingest exceeds its allocation.

mitigations.summary: Detect abnormal ingest fill rates
mitigations.detail: Alert on sustained deviations in device, fleet, normalizer, and lake write volume, and throttle the originating fleet before shared quotas are exhausted.

claims.title: Sensor readings may be intercepted between customer sites and the device gateway
claims.description: `flow:sensor-node-to-device-gateway:publish-readings` crosses from `boundary:field-network` to `boundary:ingest-edge` and carries device-identified sensor readings, but its `encryption_in_transit` attribute is unknown. If MQTT transport protection is not enabled for this hop, an attacker on a customer-site network or otherwise able to observe the boundary-crossing path can intercept the readings without authenticating to `process:device-gateway`. The captured device identifiers and readings can then be correlated with the customer assignment resolved by the gateway through `flow:device-gateway-to-device-registry:look-up-device`, supporting targeted follow-on attacks. This is conditional on the currently unverified transport-encryption attribute.

grounds.text: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:sensor-node-to-device-gateway:publish-readings`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown encryption state: the flow crosses from the customer-controlled `boundary:field-network` to the ingest edge, but the attacker must obtain an on-path position. Impact is medium because `flow:sensor-node-to-device-gateway:publish-readings` carries `pii`-tagged device readings and identifiers.

mitigations.summary: Require encrypted, mutually authenticated MQTT for device ingress
mitigations.detail: Set verified TLS 1.2+ transport protection on `flow:sensor-node-to-device-gateway:publish-readings`; use mTLS or an equivalent device-authenticated MQTT configuration so both the reading payload and endpoint identity are protected across the boundary.

claims.title: Forwarded telemetry may be intercepted between the ingest edge and analytics core
claims.description: `flow:device-gateway-to-telemetry-normalizer:forward-readings` crosses from `boundary:ingest-edge` into `boundary:analytics-core`, carries normalized sensor readings tagged as `pii`, and has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If Pub/Sub transport protection is not actually enforced for this hop, an attacker able to observe traffic at either side of the boundary can intercept accepted telemetry before `process:telemetry-normalizer` loads it into the lake. The captured records can be combined with the site-address and occupancy information later held in `store:telemetry-lake`, increasing the value of customer profiling. This finding is conditional on verification of the unknown encryption attribute.

grounds.text: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub and picked up by the telemetry normalizer

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:device-gateway-to-telemetry-normalizer:forward-readings`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown encryption state: the path crosses from the internet-facing ingest tier into analytics, but interception still requires a position on that path. Impact is medium because the flow is tagged `pii` and exposes accepted customer telemetry.

mitigations.summary: Verify encryption for the Pub/Sub hop
mitigations.detail: Configure and document TLS 1.2+ for `flow:device-gateway-to-telemetry-normalizer:forward-readings`, with authenticated service identities and no plaintext broker or sidecar segment.

claims.title: Fleet-wide device key leaves accepted readings unattributable to an individual node
claims.description: A holder of the fleet pre-shared key can submit readings through `flow:sensor-node-to-device-gateway:publish-readings` to `process:device-gateway` and later deny that a particular `entity:sensor-node` produced them. The flow crosses from the customer-controlled `boundary:field-network` into `boundary:ingest-edge`, but its stated fleet-wide credential authenticates only membership in the fleet rather than a unique device; a device identifier carried with a reading cannot make the shared authentication evidence prove which node sent it. A customer disputing a reading, occupancy event, or resulting fleet decision therefore cannot be conclusively contradicted by the authentication evidence. Second-order, accepted readings are forwarded through `flow:device-gateway-to-telemetry-normalizer:forward-readings` and loaded into `store:telemetry-lake`, so the attribution gap carries into customer data and business-critical historical telemetry.

grounds.text: The key is per fleet, not per device. Nobody has rotated it since deployment.

severity.justification: Submitting an unattributable reading requires possession of the fleet-wide pre-shared key on `flow:sensor-node-to-device-gateway:publish-readings`; the key is shared and never rotated, while deployed `entity:sensor-node` instances are outside operator physical control, making acquisition plausible but still a prerequisite. The non-unique credential undermines attribution for records loaded into the PII and business-critical telemetry in `store:telemetry-lake`, but the described harm is loss of accountability rather than disclosure, corruption, or outage.

mitigations.summary: Use a unique cryptographic identity for every sensor node
mitigations.detail: Replace the fleet-wide pre-shared key on `flow:sensor-node-to-device-gateway:publish-readings` with per-device credentials, preferably rotatable certificates or short-lived device credentials, and revoke credentials independently.

mitigations.summary: Record verified device identity with accepted telemetry
mitigations.detail: Have `process:device-gateway` retain the verified credential subject, device identifier, timestamp, action outcome, and correlation identifier with each accepted reading forwarded toward `store:telemetry-lake`; do not treat a publisher-supplied identifier as attribution evidence.

claims.title: A local attacker may impersonate a field technician to a sensor node
claims.description: `flow:field-technician-to-sensor-node:local-service-session` has `authentication: unknown`. If the local serial console does not verify a technician identity, a person with physical access at a customer site can impersonate `entity:field-technician` to `entity:sensor-node` and obtain read-write access to device configuration and diagnostics. This can provide control over an availability-critical deployed node; the claim is conditional on the undocumented console authentication state.

grounds.text: They are outside our physical control — a technician can be standing next to one with a laptop.
I don't know what authentication that console has, if any.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:field-technician-to-sensor-node:local-service-session`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown console authentication because an attacker must obtain on-site access, but the nodes are explicitly outside operator physical control. Impact is medium because the attack grants read-write configuration and diagnostic access to `entity:sensor-node`, which is tagged `availability-critical`, although the described action directly affects an individual node.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate and authorize every serial maintenance session
mitigations.detail: Require unique technician credentials or hardware-backed maintenance certificates on `flow:field-technician-to-sensor-node:local-service-session`, and enforce authorization for diagnostic versus configuration operations.

mitigations.summary: Protect local maintenance access from unattended physical attackers
mitigations.detail: Disable or lock the console outside an authenticated maintenance window and record device-side audit events for successful and failed service sessions.
